title: introduce kernel-variance prober to map per-layer sequence-length inefficiencies
author: Tomás Ortega
description: Motivation: We frequently see tail latency regressions that only appear for particular sequence-length distributions. Existing workload runners produce aggregate token-level metrics but do not attribute variance to model kernels or layers. This PR adds a 'kernel-variance prober' that runs focused microbenchmarks across sequence length windows and collects fine-grained per-kernel timing and variance profiles so we can prioritize kernel/graph-level optimizations and targeted quantization tradeoffs. Change summary: - New binary tools/bench/prober/kernel_variance_prober.py: orchestrates probing campaigns across sequence-length buckets, random seeds, and batch shapes; supports warmup/steady-state detection and adaptive sampling. - Benchmark harness extensions bench/harness/sequence_sampler.py: sequence-length aware samplers and an API to plug sampling policies into existing runners. - Profiling exporter bench/reporters/kernel_variance_reporter.go: aggregates raw kernel timing logs into per-layer heatmaps and high-variance segment reports; outputs ndjson for downstream ingestion. - Integration test bench/tests/test_kernel_variance_endtoend.py: small runtime smoke verifying consistent profiling across CPU/GPU backends. - CI job .github/workflows/benchmark-prober.yml: a lightweight workflow that runs the prober in a constrained emulation mode for PRs to prevent regression in core loops. Why this is different: instead of only measuring latency or throughput aggregates, the prober attributes variance to kernel implementations (attention, rotary, layernorm, matmul) and to sequence-length regions which helps routing, batching and kernel-selection decisions in the serving runtime. Usage notes: the prober can be invoked locally with `tools/prober/run_prober --profile-config examples/probes/length_scan.yaml`; output is an ndjson stream consumable by the reporting pipeline. Backwards compatibility: no runtime or serving changes; this is a benchmark-only change. Rollout plan: land as experimental tooling behind a feature flag; run nightly full-resolution campaigns for critical models and surface regressions in the benchmark dashboard.

review_comments: Priya Desai: Why use a fixed bucket width for sequence lengths? Suggest exposing a percentile-based bucket option to handle long-tail requests.
Tomás Ortega: Reply: added percentile-based bucketing and an adaptive mode that switches based on observed distribution (see sequence_sampler changes).
Ethan Park: CI shows a sporadic flake on the GPU smoke test (test_kernel_variance_endtoend.py::test_profile_consistency). Can we add retry logic or increase warmup?
Tomás Ortega: Reply: increased warmup and added deterministic RNG seed for the smoke CI; moved flaky path behind --ci-emulation flag. Reran CI and green.
Marta Kovacs: Suggest clarifying NDJSON schema in reporter docs and adding an example of how to import into the dashboard ingestion pipeline.
Tomás Ortega: Reply: added docs/bench/kernel-variance-prober.md with schema and ingestion steps.
release_notes: Add experimental kernel-variance prober: a benchmark tool that maps per-kernel timing variance across sequence-length buckets. Useful for prioritizing kernel optimizations and model routing rules. (experimental, no runtime change)
